About us

Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga is the leading national historic heritage agency. We operate in an environment marked by a growing interest in heritage, recognition of its social, cultural, environmental and economic benefits to our country, and awareness of its importance to national identity.

    NEW TO THE LIST 📍 Pembroke School Moveable Classroom How do you provide new classrooms during times of economic hardship? That was the question faced by the Taranaki Education Board during the Great Depression – an era of few resources and fluctuating rolls. Their solution: make the classrooms prefabricated – and portable. This example, which was constructed at the board’s New Plymouth workshop in 1930, was recently recognised as a Category 2 Historic Place (List No. 9041). It was used at Puniho School (a former Native School), Waiau School, Mangorei School and Pembroke School until 1975. Today, the classroom can be found at Taranaki Pioneer Village. It is still visited by past and current Pembroke School students and evokes powerful memories of people’s personal school experiences. Interestingly, there were at least 22 of these moveable classrooms built in Taranaki – however the fate of the other 21 is currently unknown. 🔗 Find out more via https://lnkd.in/eZHEQniN 📖 Full report by Brie Gullery and Anna Renton-Green

    ♻️ SAVE A HISTORIC DUNEDIN HOUSE A rare opportunity has emerged to relocate an 1860s house located at 56 Cargill Street, Ōtepoti Dunedin. Because of ground instability, the house can no longer remain on-site. Relocation is the most practical way to avoid demolition and give the building a future. As well as preserving the building, relocation will allow archaeologists to examine the ground beneath the house. The area is already recorded as an archaeological site, which means there is strong potential for evidence of past lives to survive beneath the ground. This isn’t a case of heritage and development being at odds – in this situation, it's created a chance to learn more about the city’s past. ☎️ Interested? Please get in touch with the agent handling the property sale, Paul Bernard of LJ Hooker, Dunedin, on 0274 376 929. 🔗 You can also find out more about the house and its history via https://lnkd.in/d3BD4fSE 📸 PICS 1.     HERITAGE CONSERVATION ♻️ Old St Paul's baptismal font Stone mason and conservator Marco Buerger and his colleague recently worked their steam cleaning magic as part of our conservation of Old St Paul's baptismal font. Carved from what may or may not be Ōamaru stone, and part of the building's story for well over a century, years of dust had dulled the font's intricate detailing. This careful work has revealed the beautiful craftsmanship once again. If you're in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington, check out the font for yourself—Old St Paul's is open daily between 10am and 4pm: https://lnkd.in/ecD-aV64 📸 Old St Paul's | HNZPT

    EVENT 🎟️ Looking backward and forward: Turnbull House enters its second century DATE: Tuesday 19 May WHERE: National Library of New Zealand (and online) WHEN: 5.30 - 7pm Join our Director Central Region Dr Jamie Jacobs as he shares the story of Turnbull House and what’s ahead for this historic building! Jamie will discuss the national significance of the building — its architecture, its connection to Alexander Turnbull and its role as a library. He’ll also explain how heritage shaped the restoration project to ensure this cultural asset is ready for its second century. This event is both in-person at the National Library in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington and online via Zoom! Registration and more info via https://lnkd.in/eFWyPr6A
